cut: Nordic 2, v1 — angle B, 'The Scoreboard', written to the one-question rule (owner, 18 Oct)
argument: Denmark's deepfake bill exempts satire and leaves the courts to decide what satire is; courts have answered that both ways since 1831, two all in this film, so Denmark's courts take the decider.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word; in Japanese a space marks a reveal segment and is never drawn

text.en: Denmark's bill bans AI copies / of your face, unless it's satire. / Who decides what's [satire]?
text.fi: Tanskan lakiesitys kieltää / tekoälykopiot kasvoistasi, / paitsi satiirissa. / Kuka päättää, mikä on [satiiria]?
text.ja: デンマークの 法案は / 顔の AIコピーを 禁じる。 風刺は 例外。 / 何が [風刺か]、 誰が 決める？

captions.source: Bill L 49, tabled 8 Oct 2026 by Culture Minister Zenia Stampe: a new §73a of the Copyright Act, no realistic digital imitation of a person's appearance, voice or movements without consent; satire, parody and political or social criticism stay allowed unless the fake is misinformation that seriously endangers others; target 1 Jan 2027 (Euronews 8 Oct; PPC Land; sn.dk). A bill, not law: the caption and the tag both say so.

text.en: The bill's answer: / the [courts], case by case.
text.ja: 法案の 答え： / [裁判所が] 個別に 判断する。

captions.source: The minister concedes the line is hard to draw; the courts decide case by case (Euronews; PPC Land; sn.dk, 8 Oct 2026).

text.en: Courts have ruled before. / 1831, mocking the king: guilty. / 1988, a parody ad: [protected].
text.fi: Oikeus on ratkaissut ennenkin. / 1831, kuninkaan pilkka: syyllinen. / 1988, parodiamainos: [suojattu].
text.ja: 裁判所は 前にも 判断した。 / 1831年、 国王の 風刺： 有罪。 / 1988年、 パロディ広告： [保護]。

captions.source: Paris assize court, 14 Nov 1831: Charles Philipon convicted of outrage against the person of the King, six months and 2,000 francs; his defence was the four-head king-to-pear sketch (Encyclopædia Universalis; Public Domain Review; Wikipedia 'Pear (caricature)'). Hustler Magazine v. Falwell, 485 U.S. 46 (24 Feb 1988): the Supreme Court reversed damages over an ad parody marked 'not to be taken seriously' (Cornell LII). The pear strip in the picture is the defence sketch, drawn at that trial.

text.en: 2024, AI fakes. / A Berlin court: no. / A California court: [yes].
text.fi: 2024, tekoälyväärennökset. / Berliinin oikeus: ei. / Kalifornian oikeus: [kyllä].
text.ja: 2024年、 AIの 偽動画。 / ベルリンの 裁判所： 不可。 / カリフォルニアの 裁判所： [可]。

captions.source: Landgericht Berlin II, 15 O 579/23 (reported 25 Feb 2024): a preliminary injunction against the art collective's AI-voiced 'chancellor' video, found not clearly recognisable as fake or satire (LTO; netzpolitik.org; FAZ via turi2). Kohls v. Bonta, E.D. Cal., 2 Oct 2024: preliminary injunction against AB 2839 in a suit over an AI parody campaign ad; struck down Aug 2025 (Tech Policy Press; court order). No faces of either politician are drawn.

text.en: Two all since 1831. / Denmark's courts take the [decider].
text.ja: 1831年から 2対2。 / [決勝点は] デンマークの 裁判所に。

captions.source: The station's line over its own image. The board is labelled CASES IN THIS FILM: the tally counts the four rulings shown, nothing more (COURTS: Paris 1831, Berlin 2024; SATIRE: Washington 1988, California 2024).

parody.en: AD PARODY — NOT TO BE TAKEN SERIOUSLY
parody.why: the small print the 1988 parody carried, on a blank poster; never the parody's content

post.en: Denmark's bill would ban AI copies of your face, unless it's satire. Who decides what's satire? The courts, case by case. Courts have ruled both ways since 1831: Paris, guilty; Washington, protected; Berlin, no; California, yes. #satire #deepfakes #Denmark
post.fi: Tanskan lakiesitys kieltäisi tekoälykopiot kasvoistasi, paitsi satiirissa. Kuka päättää, mikä on satiiria? Tuomioistuimet, tapaus kerrallaan. Ne ovat ratkaisseet molempiin suuntiin vuodesta 1831: Pariisi syyllinen, Washington suojattu, Berliini ei, Kalifornia kyllä.
post.ja: デンマークの法案は顔のAIコピーを禁じる。風刺は例外。何が風刺かは誰が決める？裁判所が個別に判断する。裁判所は1831年から両方向に判断してきた。パリは有罪、ワシントンは保護、ベルリンは不可、カリフォルニアは可。
